items.title: feat(api): detect Kiro terminal sessions
items.body:
## Description

Detect Kiro IDE terminal sessions as `kiro-terminal` when `TERM_PROGRAM` equals `kiro`, using the existing case-insensitive terminal fallback. Preserve the current detection precedence and ignore unrelated prefixes.

The terminal signal is evidenced by the installer shell-integration condition in [Kiro #7169](https://github.com/kirodotdev/Kiro/issues/7169). Dedicated Kiro CLI and GitHub Copilot signals remain unverified, so this contribution covers terminal detection and does not close the broader issue.

## Related Issues

Related to #8331

## How has this been tested?

- New positive regression cases failed before the implementation.
- Full `internal/api` tests and required Lefthook pre-commit and pre-push checks passed: build, lint with zero issues, 4,074 reverse-dependency tests with 8 skipped, and structural checks.
- Added lowercase, mixed-case and false-positive cases.
- Tested on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.1; direct Kiro runtime verification was unavailable.

AI assistance was used to prepare the change. The code received independent review and local testing.

\/copy_metadata #8331

items.title: fix(duo): keep missing binary versions empty
items.body:
## Description

Keep `InstallStatus.Version` limited to recorded version data rather than the display text `unknown version`. For custom Duo binaries without a recorded version, help displays the installed path without a version suffix. Recorded versions retain the existing version-and-path display.

Add regression coverage for custom and managed binaries with and without recorded versions, including the setup guidance for a managed binary without a recorded version.

## Related Issues

Resolves #8550

## How has this been tested?

- Binary manager, Duo and Orbit package tests passed.
- Required Lefthook pre-commit and pre-push checks passed: build, lint with zero issues, 418 tests, structural checks, and generated documentation/code without drift.
- Tested on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.1.

AI assistance was used to prepare the change. The code received independent review and local testing.

\/copy_metadata #8550

items.title: fix(glrepo): skip fork candidates without local remotes
items.body:
## Description

With prompts disabled, `glab mr create` can panic when a local fork's parent is itself a fork: `HeadRepo` selects the API-only parent and returns a typed-nil `*Remote`. Skip fork candidates whose local remote lookup fails, and preserve the existing first-remote fallback.

Add a fork-of-a-fork regression that asserts a non-nil head repository with the expected name and host. This change addresses #8567; the distinct unrelated-fork selection behavior in #8382 remains outside its scope.

## Related Issues

Resolves #8567

## How has this been tested?

- The new regression failed before the resolver change.
- `Test_HeadRepo`, required Lefthook pre-commit and pre-push checks passed.
- `make check`: 5,502 tests passed, 9 skipped. Full lint reported six existing findings in untouched documentation, Duo ask, and dependency-firewall files; lint against this branch's changes passed. The same findings were reproduced on unchanged `main`.
- Tested on macOS arm64 with Go 1.27.1.

AI assistance was used to prepare the change. The code received independent review and local testing.

\/copy_metadata #8567

issue.title: Add a way to close milestones
issue.body:
### Problem to solve

Right now you can do the basic CRUD operations on milestones, but you can not close them.

### Proposal

Add a new flag: `glab milestone edit XXX --close` that would close the given milestone.

### Further details

Our milestones work on a time based, so whenever the period finishes, we create new milestones, move open work items to the these new milestones and finally we close the old milestones.

So far we can do all of it but the last part, closing milestones.

### Links / references

items.title: `glab iteration list` header shows the page count as the total
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: `glab 1.114.0 (4d7c6cd)`, and confirmed with a build of `main` at 48512c0d (newer than v1.120.0)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 6.18.54 x86_64 (NixOS)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 19.3.3-ee
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output
  (debug mode logs only the Git calls; the request itself succeeds)

### Summary

`glab iteration list` has the same header bug as `glab label list` (#8573): it
prints the number of iterations on the current page as both the count and the
total, so the header never shows the real total. With more iterations than one
page, the header reads `Showing iteration 30 of 30`, which looks like a
complete list. This was pointed out in the review of !3991.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.18.54 x86_64
- SHELL: /run/current-system/sw/bin/zsh
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.114.0 (4d7c6cd)

Other: also checked with `glab DEV ()` built from `main` at 48512c0d.

My instance has no iterations, so live I could only observe the empty-list
header (`Showing iteration 0 of 0 ...` on both 1.114.0 and `main`). The
paginated case is confirmed from the source below and with unit tests that
mock a response with `TotalItems: 25`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a project (or group) with more iterations than one page, or pass a
   small `--per-page`.
2. Run `glab iteration list -P 1`, or `glab iteration list -g <group> -P 1`.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The second number always equals the first one, for example
`Showing iteration 1 of 1 on OWNER/REPO.` regardless of how many iterations
exist. An empty list prints `Showing iteration 0 of 0 on OWNER/REPO.`

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

The total comes from the API, as in the other list commands, for example
`Showing 1 of 25 iterations on OWNER/REPO. (Page 1)`.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

The JSON output (`-F json`) is correct. Only the header line is affected.

### Possible fixes

`internal/commands/iteration/list/iteration_list.go` passes `len(iterations)`
twice and discards the API response:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/48512c0d/internal/commands/iteration/list/iteration_list.go#L128
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/48512c0d/internal/commands/iteration/list/iteration_list.go#L148

Build the header with `utils.NewListTitle` and `resp.TotalItems`, the same way
!3991 fixed `label list`. I have a fix with tests ready and will open a merge
request.

items.title: 1.5 Show specific error messages in work-items-experimental
items.body:
Item 1.5 in the epic https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23916

## Problem

Item 1.1 shows one generic message for any failed request. Users need to know what went wrong and what to do about it. The difficulty is that the REST API returns 404 for three different reasons, deliberately: the work item doesn't exist, the user can't see it, or the `work_item_rest_api` feature flag is off. Experimental endpoints return 404 rather than 403 while the flag is off, so glab can't tell those cases apart.

## Scope

A shared error helper for all `work-items-experimental` commands, as agreed on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8582 (decision 6):

| Response | Message |
|---|---|
| 404 | Names the work item and project or group, and lists all three possible causes, including the feature flag. The PoC's `note get` already does this. |
| 401 | Not authenticated: suggest `glab auth login` or checking the token. |
| 403 | No permission. Mention that granular tokens may not cover every endpoint. |
| 400 or 422 | Show the API's message, which explains the invalid input. |
| Network errors | Unchanged from the rest of glab. |

- Keep glab's existing exit codes. Don't add new ones.
- Use the helper in `get` now, and in every later command.

## Out of scope

- Detecting whether the feature flag is on. The API gives no reliable signal. If the backend adds one, for example a distinct response or header, open a follow-up issue to use it.

## Done when

- [ ] `get` shows the messages above for each response type.
- [ ] Tests cover 400, 401, 403, 404 and 422 responses.
- [ ] The helper is shared, so later commands can use it.
- [ ] The epic's shared checklist is met.

Suggested weight: 2.

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

Depends on !4010 (item 1.1, `work-items-experimental get`) landing first.

1. Add a helper in a shared package under `internal/commands/workitemsexperimental/` (for example `utils/errors.go`), such as `func APIError(err error, what, scope string) error`. Use `errors.As(err, *gitlab.ErrorResponse)` to read `Response.StatusCode`, following `Is404` in `internal/api/client.go:540`.
2. Map statuses: 404 names the work item and project or group and lists all three causes (missing, no access, `work_item_rest_api` flag off); 401 suggests `glab auth login` or checking the token; 403 says no permission and that granular tokens may not cover every endpoint; 400 and 422 surface the API's `Message`. Return any other error (including network errors) unchanged.
3. Keep existing exit codes: wrap with `cmdutils.WrapError` (`internal/cmdutils/errors.go:76`) rather than adding new codes.
4. Replace the single `fmt.Errorf` wrap after `GetWorkItem` (which currently applies the feature flag message to every error) in `internal/commands/workitemsexperimental/get/get.go` with the helper.
5. Add table-driven tests for the helper (400, 401, 403, 404, 422, and a non-HTTP error), and extend `internal/commands/workitemsexperimental/get/get_test.go` with one case per status using the client-go mock.
6. The command is hidden, so `make gen-docs` should produce no changes; run it to confirm.

items.title: 1.4 Add --features to work-items-experimental get
items.body:
Item 1.4 in the epic https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/-/work_items/23916

## Problem

The REST API only returns a work item's widgets (REST "features") when they're requested by name. Item 1.1 requests a fixed set for the text output. Users need to choose which widgets to see, especially in JSON, and to see any of the 22 widgets the API can return.

## Scope

- **`--features`** on `get`, as agreed on https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/work_items/8582 (decision 4):
  - A comma-separated list, for example `--features labels,milestone`.
  - `all` to request every readable widget.
  - Without the flag, request the widgets the text output shows.
- **The 22 readable widgets:** `assignees`, `award_emoji`, `color`, `custom_fields`, `description`, `designs`, `development`, `error_tracking`, `health_status`, `hierarchy`, `iteration`, `labels`, `linked_items`, `milestone`, `notifications`, `progress`, `requirement_legacy`, `start_and_due_date`, `status`, `time_tracking`, `verification_status`, `weight`.
- **Validate names before sending.** The API ignores unknown values, so a typo would silently return nothing. Reject unknown names with a list of valid ones.
- **Widgets the type doesn't support:** the API leaves them out of the response. In text output, show "not available for this type" only for widgets the user requested explicitly. In JSON, leave them out, as the API does.
- **Text output:** decide how each requested widget appears. Simple widgets such as weight or health status can be one line. Complex ones such as time tracking, development or custom fields need a short summary.

## Out of scope

- `--features` on `list`, `child list` and `link list`: items in iterations 2 and 5.

## Notes

- Premium and Ultimate widgets are left out of the response on Free, the same as unsupported widgets. Make sure the message doesn't suggest the widget is missing for another reason.
- If text output for all 22 widgets is too much for one MR, split it: support every widget in JSON first, then add text output for the rest in a follow-up.

## Done when

- [ ] `get --features <list>` and `get --features all` request the right widgets.
- [ ] Unknown names are rejected with the list of valid names.
- [ ] Unsupported widgets show "not available for this type" in text output when requested.
- [ ] Each widget has a text representation, or a follow-up issue exists for the remainder.
- [ ] The tester guide (item 1.2) is updated.
- [ ] The epic's shared checklist is met.

Suggested weight: 3.

### Links / references

items.body:
This is already supported: `glab milestone edit <id> --state close` closes a milestone, and `--state activate` reopens it. It works for project milestones and, with `--group`, for group milestones. It shipped in v1.77.0 via !2536 ([flag definition](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/internal/commands/milestone/edit/edit.go#L85), [docs](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/docs/source/milestone/edit.md)). Closing as already implemented.

If you think this should remain open or be revisited, please let us know.

readme.content:
# GLab

![GLab](docs/source/img/glab-logo.png)

GLab is an open source GitLab CLI tool. It brings GitLab to your terminal, next to where you are already working with `git` and your code, without switching between windows and browser tabs. While it's powerful for issues and merge requests, `glab` does even more:

- View, manage, and retry CI/CD pipelines directly from your CLI.
- Create changelogs.
- Create and manage releases.
- Ask GitLab Duo Chat (Classic) questions about Git.
- Manage GitLab agents for Kubernetes.

`glab` is available for repositories hosted on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and GitLab Self-Managed. It supports multiple authenticated GitLab instances, and automatically detects the authenticated hostname from the remotes available in your working Git directory.

![command example](docs/source/img/getting-started.gif)

## Table of contents

- [Requirements](#requirements)
- [Usage](#usage)
  - [Commands](#commands)
  - [GitLab Duo for the CLI](#gitlab-duo-for-the-cli)
- [Demo](#demo)
- [Documentation](#documentation)
- [Installation](#installation)
  - [Homebrew](#homebrew)
  - [Other installation methods](#other-installation-methods)
  - [Building from source](#building-from-source)
    - [Prerequisites for building from source](#prerequisites-for-building-from-source)
- [Authentication](#authentication)
- [Configuration](#configuration)
- [Environment variables](#environment-variables)
  - [Debugging](#debugging)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)
- [Issues](#issues)
- [Security](#security)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
  - [Versioning](#versioning)
  - [Classify version changes](#classify-version-changes)
  - [Compatibility](#compatibility)
- [Inspiration](#inspiration)

## Requirements

`glab` officially supports GitLab versions 16.0 and later. Certain commands might require
more recent versions. While many commands might work properly in GitLab versions
15.x and earlier, no support is provided for these versions.

## Usage

To get started with `glab`:

1. Follow the [installation instructions](#installation) appropriate for your operating system.
1. [Authenticate](#authentication) into your instance of GitLab.
1. Optional. Configure `glab` further to meet your needs:
   - 1Password users can configure it to [authenticate to `glab`](https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/shell-plugins/gitlab/).
   - Set any needed global, per-project, or per-host [configuration](#configuration).
   - Set any needed [environment variables](#environment-variables).

You're ready!

### Commands

Run `glab --help` to view a list of core commands in your terminal.

<!-- commands-list-start: generated by 'make gen-docs'; do not edit by hand -->
- [`glab alias`](docs/source/alias): Create, list, and delete aliases.
- [`glab api`](docs/source/api): Make an authenticated request to the GitLab API.
- [`glab artifact-registry`](docs/source/artifact-registry): Authenticate with GitLab Artifact Registry. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab attestation`](docs/source/attestation): Manage software attestations. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab auth`](docs/source/auth): Manage authentication for glab.
- [`glab changelog`](docs/source/changelog): Generate changelogs from your project's commit history.
- [`glab check-update`](docs/source/check-update): Check for the latest glab version.
- [`glab ci`](docs/source/ci): Work with GitLab CI/CD pipelines and jobs.
- [`glab cluster`](docs/source/cluster): Manage GitLab Agents for Kubernetes and their clusters.
- [`glab completion`](docs/source/completion): Generate shell completion scripts.
- [`glab config`](docs/source/config): Manage glab settings.
- [`glab container-registry`](docs/source/container-registry): Work with GitLab container registries.
- [`glab dependency-firewall`](docs/source/dependency-firewall): Configure and monitor GitLab Dependency Firewall for local package managers. (EXPERIMENTAL)
- [`glab deploy-key`](docs/source/deploy-key): Manage deploy keys.
- [`glab duo`](docs/source/duo): Work with GitLab Duo.

Commands follow this pattern:

```shell
glab <command> <subcommand> [flags]
```

Many core commands also have sub-commands. Some examples:

- List merge requests assigned to you: `glab mr list --assignee=@me`
- List review requests for you: `glab mr list --reviewer=@me`
- Approve a merge request: `glab mr approve 235`
- Create an issue, and add milestone, title, and label: `glab issue create -m release-2.0.0 -t "My title here" --label important`

### GitLab Duo for the CLI

The GitLab CLI also includes support for using the GitLab Duo Agent Platform directly in your terminal.

Use `glab duo cli` to ask GitLab Duo questions about your codebase and to autonomously perform actions on your behalf.

For more information, see [GitLab Duo CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/gitlab_duo_cli/).

## Demo

[![asciicast](https://asciinema.org/a/368622.svg)](https://asciinema.org/a/368622)

## Documentation

Read the [documentation](docs/source/_index.md) for usage instructions or check out `glab help`.

## Installation

Download a binary suitable for your OS at the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases).
Other installation methods depend on your operating system.

### Homebrew

Homebrew is the officially supported package manager for macOS, Linux, and Windows (through [Windows Subsystem for Linux](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/install))

- Homebrew
  - Install with: `brew install glab`
  - Update with: `brew upgrade glab`

### Other installation methods

Other options to install the GitLab CLI that may not be officially supported or are maintained by the community are [also available](docs/installation_options.md).

### Building from source

If a supported binary for your OS is not found at the [releases page](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases), you can build from source:

#### Prerequisites for building from source

- `make`
- Go version as defined by [`main/go.mod`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/go.mod?ref_type=heads#L3)

To build from source:

1. Run `go version` to verify that you have the minimum required Go version.
   If Go is not installed, see [Download and install](https://go.dev/doc/install).
1. Clone the repository: `git clone https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli.git`
1. Build the binary: `make build`
1. Install `glab` in `$GOPATH/bin`: `make install`
1. Optional. If `$GOPATH/bin` or `$GOBIN` is not in your `$PATH`,
   run `export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH`.
1. Confirm the installation: `glab version`

## Authentication

To authenticate `glab` with OAuth, a personal access token, or a CI job token, see
[Authenticate with GitLab](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/).

## Configuration

For configuration levels, the configuration search order, and platform-specific file
locations, see [Configure the CLI](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/configuration/).

For connecting to a GitLab Self-Managed or GitLab Dedicated instance, and for mTLS and
self-signed certificates, see
[Connect to your GitLab instance](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/connection/).

For authenticating proxies, including custom HTTP headers and Google Identity-Aware
Proxy, see [Connect through a proxy](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/proxies/).

## Environment variables

`glab` reads its configuration from environment variables as well as the configuration
file. Every configuration key has a matching variable, and the variable wins over the
stored value. Setting them centrally is a good way to give everyone in an organization
the same setup.

For the full reference, see
[Environment variables](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/configuration/#environment-variables).
For how `glab` picks which token to use, see
[Token precedence](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/#token-precedence).

### Debugging

When the `GLAB_DEBUG` environment variable is set to `true`, `glab` outputs more logging information, including:

- Underlying Git commands.
- Expanded aliases.
- DNS error details.

## Troubleshooting

For help with common authentication issues, see
[Troubleshooting](https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/authentication/#troubleshooting) in the GitLab CLI documentation.

## Issues

If you have an issue: report it on the [issue tracker](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues)

## Security

To report a security vulnerability in `glab`, follow the process in
the [security policy](SECURITY.md). Please do not open a public issue.

To learn how the project handles dependency updates and container-scanner CVE
reports, see [dependency management](CONTRIBUTING.md#dependency-management)
and [reporting a vulnerability](CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-a-vulnerability)
in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

## Contributing

Feel like contributing? That's awesome! We have a [contributing guide](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of conduct](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) to help guide you.

When updating command help text or documentation, follow the
[GitLab CLI documentation style guide](https://docs.gitlab.com/development/documentation/cli_styleguide/).

### Versioning

This project follows the [SemVer](https://github.com/semver/semver) specification.

### Classify version changes

- If deleting a command, changing how it behaves, or adding a new **required** flag, the release must use a new `MAJOR` revision.
- If adding a new command or **optional** flag, the release must use a new `MINOR` revision.
- If fixing a bug, the release must use a new `PATCH` revision.

### Compatibility

We do our best to introduce breaking changes only when releasing a new `MAJOR` version.
Unfortunately, there are situations where this is not possible, and we may introduce
a breaking change in a `MINOR` or `PATCH` version. Some of situations where we may do so:

- If a security issue is discovered, and the solution requires a breaking change,
  we may introduce such a change to resolve the issue and protect our users.
- If a feature was not working as intended, and the bug fix requires a breaking change,
  the bug fix may be introduced to ensure the functionality works as intended.
- When feature behavior is overwhelmingly confusing due to a vague specification
  on how it should work. In such cases, we may refine the specification
  to remove the ambiguity, and introduce a breaking change that aligns with the
  refined specification. For an example of this, see
  [merge request 1382](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/1382#note_1686888887).
- Experimental features are not guaranteed to be stable, and can be modified or
  removed without a breaking change.

Breaking changes are a last resort, and we try our best to only introduce them when absolutely necessary.

## Inspiration

The GitLab CLI was adopted from [Clement Sam](https://gitlab.com/profclems) in 2022 to serve as the official CLI of GitLab. Over the years the project has been inspired by both the [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli) and [Zaq? Wiedmann's](https://gitlab.com/zaquestion) [lab](https://github.com/zaquestion/lab).

Lab has served as the foundation for many of the GitLab CI/CD commands including `ci view` and `ci trace`.

items.title: Follow-up from "fix(orbit): forward --help to the Orbit binary once it is installed"
items.body:
The following discussions from !3892 should be addressed:

- [ ] @phikai started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3892#note_3831356299): 

    > Non-blocking, but worth recording: the shared `InstalledBinary` also tightens duo. `Installed` now requires a non-empty `duo_cli_binary_version` for a managed install, where `main` only stat-ed the path. With the managed binary on disk and no recorded version, I get `installed=false` here against `installed=true` on `main`, so the footer flips to "not installed yet" plus the three install steps.
    > 
    > That is the more accurate answer, since `EnsureInstalled` would re-download in that state, and `binarymgr` covers it in "managed binary without a recorded version is not installed". Two follow-ups:
    > 
    > - The duo suite only exercises the custom-path branch (`TestBinaryStatus` sets `GLAB_DUO_CLI_BINARY_PATH`), so nothing in `internal/commands/duo/cli` pins the managed-path behavior. A managed-path case next to the existing "unknown version" one would lock it in.
    > - The description says duo just reuses the moved check. Calling out the footer change would help whoever bisects it later.

- [ ] @phikai started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3892#note_3831356502): 

    > Optional: `InstallStatus.Version` now carries display text. `"unknown version"` is what the duo footer prints, and it means a consumer cannot tell "no version recorded" from a real version string. Orbit does not read `Version` at all.
    > 
    > Returning `""` and keeping the fallback in `AppendBinaryStatusFooter` would keep `binarymgr` free of user-facing strings. It also removes the mild oddity in the new tests, where `InstallStatus{Version: "unknown version", Installed: true}` is the expected value for a binary whose version is genuinely unknown.

- [ ] @phikai started a [discussion](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/merge_requests/3892#note_3831435650): 

    > Version 3 addresses everything I raised, and I verified the behavior rather than just the diff: help renders instead of erroring with a stale managed binary in CI, no consent prompt or update check on the help path, and the duo footer matches `main` again when a config key cannot be read. Docs regenerate with no drift.
    > 
    > The two threads I left today are not blocking. Would be good to see them in a follow-up:
    > 
    > - a managed-path case in the duo `TestBinaryStatus` set, so nothing in `internal/commands/duo/cli` can silently flip the footer
    > - moving the `unknown version` fallback out of `binarymgr` and into the footer, ideally with wording that fits custom-path users, who are now the main audience for that string
    > 
    > Approving from my side.

<!-- implementation plan added during 2026-09 backlog triage -->

## Implementation plan

> **Note:** This plan was drafted during an AI-assisted triage of the backlog and has not been validated by a maintainer. Treat it as a starting point: file paths, line numbers, and the approach may need adjusting.

Two independent changes from !3892. They can land together or separately.

1. **Return an empty version from `binarymgr`.** In `internal/binarymgr/runner.go`, delete the `if status.Version == "" { status.Version = "unknown version" }` block at lines 241-243 so `InstallStatus.Version` carries only a real recorded version. `internal/commands/orbit/orbit.go:134` reads only `Path` and `Installed`, so it needs no change.

2. **Move the display fallback into the duo footer.** In `internal/commands/duo/cli/cli.go`, handle the empty version where the footer is rendered (`binaryStatus` at line 129, or the installed branch at lines 109-113). Because a managed binary with no recorded version now reports `Installed: false`, the only way to reach this line is a custom `duo_cli_binary_path`, where glab never records a version. Print `Installed: <path>` with no parenthetical in that case, rather than carrying "unknown version" forward; if the maintainer prefers to keep a parenthetical, "version not recorded" reads better than "unknown version" for a user-supplied binary.

3. **Update the `binarymgr` expectations.** In `internal/binarymgr/runner_test.go`, change the two assertions that expect `Version: "unknown version"` (lines 144 and 190) to expect `Version: ""`.

4. **Add a managed-path case to the duo suite.** In `internal/commands/duo/cli/cli_test.go`, add a subtest to `TestBinaryStatus` (line 278) that does not set `GLAB_DUO_CLI_BINARY_PATH`. Follow `managedSetup` in `internal/binarymgr/runner_test.go:116`: `t.Setenv("GLAB_CONFIG_DIR", t.TempDir())`, resolve `binarymgr.ManagedBinaryPath(Spec())`, write an executable file there, set `duo_cli_binary_version` on a blank config, and assert `installed` is true with that version. Add a sibling case with the version key unset that asserts `installed` is false, which is the footer flip !3892 introduced.

5. **Cover the footer wording.** Extend `internal/commands/duo/cli/cli_test.go` next to `TestAppendBinaryStatusFooter_ShowsSetupStepsWhenNotInstalled` (line 316) with an installed case that asserts the exact line the footer prints for a custom path with no recorded version.

6. **Verify.** `go test ./internal/binarymgr/... ./internal/commands/duo/... ./internal/commands/orbit/...`. No cobra `Short`, `Long`, `Example`, or flag text changes, so `make gen-docs` is not needed.

items.title: mr create: nil *Remote panic in non-interactive HeadRepo resolution when fork parent is itself a fork
items.body:
### Summary

`glab mr create` panics with a nil `*Remote` when it can't prompt (no TTY, e.g. scripts or AI agents) and the fork parent of the current project is itself a fork.

In the non-interactive branch of `ResolvedRemotes.HeadRepo`, glab selects the **first** project in the network that has `ForkedFromProject != nil`. Here that is the parent, not the local project. The parent has no local git remote, so `RemoteForRepo` returns `(nil, err)`. The error is discarded and the typed-nil `*Remote` is returned as a non-nil `Interface`:

```go
// internal/glrepo/resolver.go (v1.113.0), ~L245
if repoMap[repo].ForkedFromProject != nil {
    selectedRepoInfo, _ := FromFullName((repoMap[repo].HTTPURLToRepo), r.defaultHostname, r.cfg)
    remote, _ := r.RemoteForRepo(selectedRepoInfo)
    return remote, nil
}
```

`mr_create.go:387` then calls `headRepo.FullName()` on it and panics.

The interactive path already handles `remote == nil` by falling back to `r.remotes[0]` with a `head:<path>` resolution. The non-interactive path has no such fallback. This is related to #8422 but not the same bug: there the parent lookup fails, here it succeeds.

### Environment

- OS: Linux (WSL2)
- GLAB: 1.113.0 (d62881304)
- Invoked without a TTY

### Steps to reproduce

1. Project chain: `group/base` <- fork `group/sub/template` <- fork `group/sub/project`.
2. Clone `group/sub/project`, with only `origin` as a remote.
3. Push a branch and run without a TTY:
   `glab mr create --target-branch main --source-branch my-branch --title t --description x < /dev/null | cat`

### What is the current bug behavior?

```
panic: value method gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/glrepo.Remote.FullName called using nil *Remote pointer

gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/glrepo.(*Remote).FullName(0x30?)
	<autogenerated>:1 +0x2f
gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/mr/create.(*options).run(...)
	gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/internal/commands/mr/create/mr_create.go:387 +0x255
```

With `--yes`, it fails the same way.

### What is the expected correct behavior?

The head repo should resolve to the project behind `origin`, the only local remote. No panic.

### Possible fixes

- In the non-interactive loop, only consider repos that have a local remote. Or check the `RemoteForRepo` error and continue to the next repo.
- At minimum, don't return a typed-nil `*Remote` as an `Interface`. Fall back to `r.remotes[0]` as the interactive path does.

Workaround: `glab mr create --head <group/sub/project> ...`, or create the MR via `glab api POST projects/:id/merge_requests`.

items.title: `glab iteration list` header shows the page count as the total
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: `glab 1.114.0 (4d7c6cd)`, and confirmed with a build of `main` at 48512c0d (newer than v1.120.0)
- [x] Operating system and version: Linux 6.18.54 x86_64 (NixOS)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed instance
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed) 19.3.3-ee
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [x] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output
  (debug mode logs only the Git calls; the request itself succeeds)

### Summary

`glab iteration list` has the same header bug as `glab label list` (#8573): it
prints the number of iterations on the current page as both the count and the
total, so the header never shows the real total. With more iterations than one
page, the header reads `Showing iteration 30 of 30`, which looks like a
complete list. This was pointed out in the review of !3991.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.18.54 x86_64
- SHELL: /run/current-system/sw/bin/zsh
- TERM: xterm-256color
- GLAB: glab 1.114.0 (4d7c6cd)

Other: also checked with `glab DEV ()` built from `main` at 48512c0d.

My instance has no iterations, so live I could only observe the empty-list
header (`Showing iteration 0 of 0 ...` on both 1.114.0 and `main`). The
paginated case is confirmed from the source below and with unit tests that
mock a response with `TotalItems: 25`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a project (or group) with more iterations than one page, or pass a
   small `--per-page`.
2. Run `glab iteration list -P 1`, or `glab iteration list -g <group> -P 1`.

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The second number always equals the first one, for example
`Showing iteration 1 of 1 on OWNER/REPO.` regardless of how many iterations
exist. An empty list prints `Showing iteration 0 of 0 on OWNER/REPO.`

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

The total comes from the API, as in the other list commands, for example
`Showing 1 of 25 iterations on OWNER/REPO. (Page 1)`.

### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

The JSON output (`-F json`) is correct. Only the header line is affected.

### Possible fixes

`internal/commands/iteration/list/iteration_list.go` passes `len(iterations)`
twice and discards the API response:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/48512c0d/internal/commands/iteration/list/iteration_list.go#L128
- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/48512c0d/internal/commands/iteration/list/iteration_list.go#L148

Build the header with `utils.NewListTitle` and `resp.TotalItems`, the same way
!3991 fixed `label list`. I have a fix with tests ready and will open a merge
request.
